Calculate the pressure distribution inside a centrifuge using the rotating-fluid equilibrium equation dP/dr = ρ · r · ω².
Integrate this equation from the axis of rotation outward with the boundary condition P(r = 0) = 0, meaning pressure is treated as gauge pressure with zero reference at the axis.
Leave the fluid density ρ as a symbolic variable throughout; do not substitute any specific fluid or numerical density value.
Set the rotational speed to 10,000 RPM and convert to angular velocity as ω = 10,000 × 2π / 60 rad/s, which evaluates to approximately 1047.2 rad/s.
Present the final result as the closed-form expression P(r) = ½ ρ ω² r², showing it both with ω carried symbolically and with ω ≈ 1047.2 rad/s substituted, so the reader can see the numerical prefactor.
The domain of the expression is r ranging from 0 outward with no upper radius limit; present P as a continuous function of r over that domain.
Do not include any atmospheric pressure offset, imposed back-pressure, or additional terms; the result represents only the pure centrifugal contribution to pressure.
Format the writeup so a competent engineer or physicist can reproduce the integration steps, verify the substitution of ω, and evaluate P at any chosen radius by simply plugging in their own value of ρ and r.
